report.question: Can a work-unit output satisfy all 12 numbered conditions of the shared completion predicate and still be unusable by its declared downstream consumer?
report.answer: CONFIRMED on the reconstructed field-reader that implements the published c12 algorithm, and CONFIRMED as decorative by P12-ADVERSARIAL-REFUTATION.md on this tree. The canonical module is absent here. 5 constructed attacks are COMPLETE under the field-reader and unreadable under Probe 2. ADV-9000 passes both.
report.mechanism: semantic-gap attack: satisfy every syntactic condition while violating the intent of condition 12. The gap is that conditions 4 and 12 measure two different things and neither measures the one that matters - condition 4 validates the artifact against the schema THE CALLER SUPPLIES, condition 12 validates the RECEIPT'S ASSERTION about a consumer. Nothing validates the artifact against what the consumer actually requires.

report.smallest_fix: Condition 12 must not read the receipt. The reducer should RUN the declared consumer against the artifact and take the observed exit code, exactly as the reducer already re-hashes the artifact rather than trusting the declared sha256 - the identical design move the same file already makes for conditions 2 and 3. If executing a consumer inside the reducer is undesirable, the second-best is to make condition 12 NOT-CHECKED whenever the consumer's raw_output was not produced by the reducer itself, so a self-declaration can never read as SATISFIED. Either way, condition 4 should validate against the artifact's CLASS schema resolved the way schema_resolver.py resolves it, not against whatever schema the caller happens to pass.
report.honest_limits: UNVERIFIED inline: the fixtures were fabricated by me, so this proves the predicate ACCEPTS such an output, not that any real unit has shipped one - a census of real receipts against these six shapes is the settling experiment. The harness itself failed twice before it measured anything - v1's artifact bodies were minimal so condition 4 failed for all seven cases INCLUDING the control, and the first strict-JSON consumer (jq) did not discriminate. Both failures are recorded above rather than deleted; a harness whose control also fails is measuring nothing, and I would have reported a false result had the negative control not been mandatory. Most pointedly, THIS unit's own downstream_consumers block was written as a plausible claim and was FALSE: executing it returned exit 1 on 'artifact_class was unexpected'. Had I followed the pattern this record criticises - declaring the consumer instead of running it - this artifact would have shipped schema-invalid while asserting SUCCESS:schema-valid, and the predicate would have scored it 12/12.
